Screen reader users hear "button" with no indication of its purpose, making it impossible to identify or dismiss a specific file. Voice control users cannot activate an unnamed button by speaking its label. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Go to https://apply.ruralgrants.example.gov/application/step-2 2. Navigate to the uploaded documents list within the form 3. Open NVDA (or VoiceOver on macOS) 4. Press Tab to move focus to the third button in the list 5. Listen to what the screen reader announces ### Expected Behaviour Screen reader announces "Remove document, button" or equivalent meaningful label. ### Actual Behaviour Screen reader announces "button" only. No accessible name is provided. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Chrome 126 | | OS | macOS 14.5 | | Screen reader | VoiceOver (default) | | Testing tool | axe-core 4.9.1 | ### Impact Blind and low-vision users relying on screen readers cannot identify or operate the remove button. Users who rely on voice control software (e.g., Dragon NaturallySpeaking, macOS Voice Control) cannot activate an unnamed button by speaking its label. This blocks a core task in the application workflow. ### Suggested Fix Add an accessible name to the ` ```
